title: Switch the coding agent on, off, or have it slip in a bug
text:
In short
The coding agent now switches on or off for each task, and in Interview the interviewer can have it slip in a bug to see who reviews the code and who copy-pastes it. Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol reached Codility within 4 days of launch, and Screen and Interview reports show a proficiency level for each skill.
19 more releases shipped in September 2026, listed in the table below.
Screen and Interview reports now show a level for every skill.
Find the right task using AI recommends tasks from a job description.
AI for Business now runs in live interviews, and the Task Randomizer fills task pools in one click.

AI on or off for each task, a coding agent you can steer, and new models
AI Assistance now switches on or off for each task in Screen and Skills Intelligence. One assessment can ask a candidate to build a feature with Claude Code, then fix a bug without AI.
In Interview, interviewers can now write AI Instructions that the AI Copilot and Claude Code follow, and candidates do not see them. Ask the agent to slip in a bug or a poor coding practice, and you see in real time whether the candidate reviews the code or copy-pastes it. Every prompt, command and code change is saved to the report, for each task where AI is on.
Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.5 on September 28 and OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Sol on September 29. We had both live in Codility on October 2. Claude Sonnet 5.5 is now in Claude Code, the AI Copilot and the AI Assistant chat. GPT-6.1 Sol is in the AI Copilot in Interview, and the AI Copilot also adds GPT-6 Luna.
Read why
detecting AI use is the wrong hiring question
See where coding agents belong in your assessments
An admin switches AI Assistance on in account settings, and from there every task carries its own choice. Talk to us and we will walk your team through an assessment that tests how candidates direct a coding agent and what they can do alone.
Talk to us

Screen and Interview reports now show each skill a candidate demonstrated, with its proficiency level out of 5, next to the highest level the assessment could measure.
Tasks from a job description.

Random task sets in seconds.
The Task Randomizer now suggests tasks for each pool, fills every pool in one click and sits inside assessment creation. It is in Closed preview.
AI for Business in live interviews.
AI for Business, Codility’s assessment for roles beyond engineering, now runs in Interview, in a text editor candidate and interviewer share in real time.
Remote access detection.
Codility Desktop flags an active remote access session in the report, for sessions with Device Integrity on.
Everything that shipped in September
Every release from September 2026, whether or not it appears above. 20 entries.
AI Assistance switches on or off for each task
One assessment can now test how a candidate works with a coding agent and what they can do alone. AI Assistance has its own switch on every task in Screen and Skills Intelligence, and each task card shows exactly what the candidate gets. Every interaction stays in the Candidate Report for each task where AI is on.
What’s New
An AI Assistance switch on every task card in Screen and Skills Intelligence
A tag on each card showing what the candidate gets: AI Copilot and Claude Code Terminal for VS Code tasks, AI Assistant Chat for Basic IDE tasks
Hover the AI Copilot tag to see the available modes and models
Tasks that require AI, such as AI for Business tasks, stay on and are marked as such
Settings follow your Screen defaults, including locks set for the account
Settings can be adjusted until the first candidate is invited
Availability
Live for all accounts, in Screen and Skills Intelligence. In Interview, AI is set for each interview.
Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, within 4 days of launch
Candidates work with AI tools closer to the ones they would use at work. Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.5 on September 28 and OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Sol on September 29, and both were live in Codility on October 2. Claude Code, the AI Copilot and the AI Assistant chat now use Claude Sonnet 5.5, the AI Copilot adds 2 GPT models, and Claude Code itself has been updated. The AI Assistant chat now uses the same model in every region.
Claude Sonnet 5.5 replaces Claude Sonnet 4.5 in Claude Code and the AI Copilot
In the AI Copilot, GPT-6 Luna replaces GPT-4o mini, and GPT-6.1 Sol replaces GPT-5 mini, in Interview only
Claude Code in the VS Code terminal has been updated
The AI Assistant chat uses Claude Sonnet 5.5 in both the EU and the US
AI usage reports recognize the new models, so token and interaction counts stay complete
Live wherever AI Assistance is on. Existing settings and premium model access are unchanged.
Steer the coding agent during a live interview
Interviewers can now steer the coding agent during a live interview. Tell the AI Copilot or Claude Code to slip in a bug or a poor coding practice, then see whether the candidate reviews the code or copy-pastes it. Or match the agent to how your own team works with AI. A new AI Instructions tab, visible only to interviewers, sets instructions both agents follow. Autocomplete usage is now also part of AI Usage Insights for every customer.
An AI Instructions tab next to the task description, visible only to interviewers
Click Apply to use the instructions with both the AI Copilot and Claude Code
The AI Copilot picks up changes immediately, and Claude Code uses them from its next new conversation
Instructions are shared across interviewers and saved within the session
Autocomplete usage now included in AI Usage Insights
Live for all customers, in Interview. Instructions are not yet saved with custom tasks.
Skills proficiency in Screen and Interview reports
Hiring managers get a skill-level signal they can act on. Screen and Interview reports now show which skills a candidate demonstrated and the level reached in each, on the same award-winning proficiency scale as Skills Intelligence. The highest level the assessment could measure sits beside each skill, which is designed to keep the read fair.
A Skills proficiency section on Screen and Interview reports, with search, filters and sorting
Each skill on a five-level proficiency scale, viewable for the whole assessment and per task
The highest level each assessment could measure, shown for every skill
Scored automatically once an assessment is evaluated or an interview closes, for Basic IDE and VS Code tasks
Included in shared links, the PDF report and reports attached to applicant tracking systems
When nothing can be scored, the report explains why
In Open preview, so it is on for every account. Only library tasks with skill tags are scored. Whiteboard, Miro, text and free-coding environments in Interview are not.
The Task Randomizer suggests alternatives, inside assessment creation
Building a balanced random assessment no longer takes deep knowledge of the library. The Task Randomizer now suggests similar tasks, fills every pool in one action and opens right inside assessment creation, through a Randomize tasks toggle, for new and existing assessments.
An Add alternatives menu: closest matches automatically, a list of suggested similar tasks, or the task library with the original task’s difficulty and time limit applied
Auto-fill all pools populates every pool in one action
A Randomize tasks toggle in the Order Tasks step, when creating or editing an assessment
Pool selections save automatically on the next step, with a warning before going back
A redesigned interface matching the Task Library’s search
The existing Randomize tasks option in assessment settings stays available
In Closed preview, for accounts with the Task Randomizer switched on. To have it switched on, contact support@codility.com or your account manager.
Find the right tasks from a job description
Picking tasks for a new role no longer depends on knowing the task library. One of the most requested features, it is now the first option when creating an assessment: Find the right task using AI takes the job description, shows the technologies and skills it found, and recommends tasks from the Codility library and your own.
Find the right task using AI, the first option in the Create an assessment dialog
Add a job description and get recommended tasks
Review and edit the technologies and skills it identified before getting recommendations
Recommendations include tasks your own team created
If a description is too thin, it says what is missing
Live wherever AI features are on for the account. Start a new assessment to try it.
AI for Business tasks run in live interviews
AI for Business brings Codility to every role beyond engineering, with real work done alongside an AI assistant and scored by fixed rules. It runs inside the same Screen, Interview and Skills Intelligence, for hiring into business roles and for assessing current business teams. Its tasks now run in live interviews, in a text editor that candidate and interviewer share in real time.
AI for Business tasks available in Interview
Real-time typing on both sides, with no blinking or jumping
A colored cursor with each person’s name
Undo reverses only your own changes
Text is kept if the connection drops and returns
Reports look the same as before
AI for Business is in Open preview, so it is on for every account. The shared text editor is live in Interview.
A clearer AI Copilot view for interviewers
Interviewers can follow the candidate’s work with the AI Copilot and keep their attention on the interview. The chat now shows when the candidate is typing a prompt, and the settings an interviewer does not need are less prominent.
An indicator at the top of the chat when the candidate is typing a prompt
Disabled fields with tooltips, so it is clear which areas are not interactive
Agent and model selection redesigned so the settings that matter to the interviewer stand out
Live, in Interview.
The Screen report inside a live interview
The interview starts from the code the candidate actually wrote. Any interviewer can now bring a candidate’s Screen report into the interview room, with nobody setting it up in advance, and each task opens in the language the candidate used.
A Screening report tile next to Templates in an empty interview room, with a searchable list of finished Screen reports
A Suggested for this interview card with this candidate’s report, attached in one click
Every task arrives with the candidate’s solution, even after the candidate has joined
Each task opens in the candidate’s language with their code in the editor, including interviews created from a Screen report
Live for all customers in Interview. Anyone who can already see Screen reports in their account can use it.
Several technology-agnostic tasks in one interview
Interviews can be structured the way a team wants to run them. A technology-agnostic task can now fill every task slot of an interview, for open-ended conversations, system design or any exercise not tied to a language.
A technology-agnostic task available in every task slot
Every technology-agnostic task used appears in the report
Live for all accounts in Interview, in the Basic IDE technology-agnostic environment.
Remote access detection in Codility Desktop
Remote control of a candidate’s machine is a common route to outside help during an assessment. Codility Desktop now detects an active remote access session and flags it in the session report, designed to give reviewers clear visibility of that kind of attempt.
Codility Desktop detects active remote access sessions
A new Remote access signal in the session report
Pattern Detection now flags retyping from another screen or device at a lower threshold
For all customers using Device Integrity in their sessions. Device Integrity is in Open preview.
A more accurate suspiciously short time signal
Flags on the Integrity Risk report are more accurate, especially on VS Code, AI for Business and customer-authored tasks. The short-time threshold now comes from real solve times for each task, where it had fallen back to a flat 2 minutes for most tasks.
Thresholds derived from real solve-time data per task
Tasks without enough history use 10% of their recommended time
Multiple-choice questions are no longer flagged
Assessments scored zero no longer pull a task’s average down
The statistics behind the signal now cover far more of the library
Live. The signal points a reviewer at a session and decides nothing on its own.
The Codility MCP server for your own AI assistant
Ask the AI assistant you already use about your assessment data. The Codility MCP server connects Claude, ChatGPT or another assistant to your account through MCP, the standard way AI assistants link to other software, so you can ask for sessions, candidate histories and test results, or an export, and repeat a report on a schedule.
Find sessions by date and status, and list candidates with test, score and report link
Open one candidate’s profile with every session they sat
Search assessments and list a folder of assessments
Download a session report as a CSV or Excel file, with the per-task breakdown
Browser sign-in, with no API keys to manage, and separate US and EU connections
Read-only, using the signed-in person’s own permissions
In Closed preview. To ask about access, contact support@codility.com or your account manager.
SystemVerilog and a Hardware Engineer role
Codility can now assess engineers who design chips, for semiconductors, telecom and networking equipment, aerospace and defense, automotive electronics and AI accelerators. 15 SystemVerilog tasks arrived with a Hardware Engineer role in the task library, and teams can build their own SystemVerilog tasks.
3 Starter Library tasks: a priority encoder, an ALU with signed and unsigned flags, and a pipelined multiply-accumulate
12 Core Library tasks, from counters and state machines to a UART transmitter, an AXI4-Lite subordinate and a small multicycle CPU
A Hardware Engineer role in the task library
SystemVerilog in the self-serve content editor and the task creation MCP server
Live, available according to your packages.
Everyday work with an AI assistant can now be screened in minutes, for business hiring in any role. 20 new tasks take about 5 to 15 minutes each, at elementary to easy difficulty and suited to any role, for assessments where 30 or more minutes of task time was the blocker.
10 everyday prompting tasks, such as drafting an agenda, warming up a blunt email or summarizing for an executive
10 inbox scenarios, each a messy moment that needs one written message, such as a double booking or a deadline pulled forward
Live for all customers. Included in your plan.
Modern Java, a paired build and new VS Code tasks
New tasks show whether an engineer can bring old code up to date, and add performance tasks that measure more than speed. More than 40 new tasks shipped across September, counting SystemVerilog and the short AI for Business tasks.
Java 8 to Java 21 modernization tasks on sealed interfaces, records, pattern matching and the SequencedMap API, each for both editors
A VS Code task that turns a single-player inventory grid into a co-op one over WebSocket
A frontend and backend task pair on one shared design, both technology-agnostic
2 library favorites moved to VS Code, and 2 performance tasks that count function calls in 9 languages
Real-life C# tasks run on .NET 10
Candidates write against current C# and .NET 10 APIs, on runtimes that are supported. Every real-life C# task moved to .NET 10, with MySQL and PowerShell updated to long-term support releases. The team checked every changed task against its recorded results, solution by solution and test by test.
56 C# tasks on .NET 10, supported until November 2028
MySQL 8.4 and PowerShell 7.6, both long-term support releases
Task descriptions list the library versions the tasks run on
The old versions are replaced
Live for all real-life C# tasks, except 4 calculator sample tasks that keep their versions and 8 Interview and technology-agnostic tasks that stay on .NET 9 for now.
Submitted tasks close, and coding environments are freed up sooner
Candidates get one clear flow in both editors, and coding environments are freed up sooner during large hiring rounds. A submitted task is now marked complete and closed in Basic IDE and VS Code alike, which releases its environment straight after scoring.
A completed badge on submitted tasks, which can no longer be opened
A submit dialog that states the solution cannot be viewed or edited afterwards
A submitted VS Code task releases its environment after scoring
Assessments with several VS Code tasks start each one by hand
When demand peaks, candidates wait to start until an environment is free
Live for all accounts.
A collapsible solution panel in every product
Candidates and interviewers get more room for the part of the session they are working in. The code editor now folds away the same way the task description does, in every product, on both VS Code and the Basic IDE.
A collapsible solution panel in every session where it appears
Headers, arrows and spacing aligned whichever panels are collapsed
What’s New in the app sidebar
What changed in Codility is now one click away from the product. The app sidebar carries a What’s New link that opens these product updates.
A What’s New item at the bottom of the app sidebar
Frequently asked questions
